Definition: good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
BiblicalUsage: Good is the first verdict God speaks over His work. He saw the light, that it was good, and He saw everything He had made, and behold, it was very good; the psalmist says, taste and see that the Lord is good; and Micah says what is good is to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that good is not a feeling but a verdict: God declares it over creation, the psalmist tastes it in the Lord, and Micah turns it into a life. I believe the word asks me to measure everything by that same verdict — what God calls good is good, and what He does not, I must not call good either.
